answer: Stake-weighted identity bonds resist sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit, say 50 credits, in escrow for 30 days before its votes or ratings count. Slashing applies if it is caught colluding, such as when onyx-style clusters of wallets rate each other in a closed loop. A graph audit flags dense, low-outside-contact groups. An attacker running 1,000 fake identities must lock 50,000 credits, forfeits it on detection, and faces a dune of idle capital. Weight grows with the square root of stake, so splitting funds across a ridge of accounts gains nothing.
